title: courier.notification.queued payload
description: THE BREAKAGE, AND IT IS ACROSS SERVICES. billing reserved `invoice_id` — its own manifest says so, on billing's own surface. courier here publishes `invoice_id` in a completely unrelated payload, for an unrelated reason, with no knowledge of the reservation. Both services are internally consistent; both schemas are valid; no document is wrong about itself. A courier consumer that generated source against a billing-shaped `invoice_id` and upgraded would bind to courier's field under the name it already trusted. This is the finding that has to name BOTH services and the name, because a message naming only one of them sends the reader to the file that is not the problem.

invoice_id.description: The invoice this notification is about. Perfectly reasonable in isolation, and it is billing's reserved name — which is the entire problem.

notification_id.description: The notification's own row id, and equal to the envelope's subject.
